5:1.sourceText: Πᾶς ὁ πιστεύων ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ἐστιν ὁ Χριστὸς ἐκ τοῦ Θεοῦ γεγέννηται, καὶ πᾶς ὁ ἀγαπῶν τὸν γεννήσαντα ἀγαπᾷ τὸν γεγεννημένον ἐξ αὐτοῦ.
5:1.targetText: Everyone who is believing that Jesus is the Christ has been begotten of God, and everyone who is loving Him who begot, also loves him who is begotten of Him.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: The additional also before loves is not separately represented in the pinned Greek; the actual earlier καί coordinates and everyone, not this extra adverb.

5:2.sourceText: ἐν τούτῳ γινώσκομεν ὅτι ἀγαπῶμεν τὰ τέκνα τοῦ Θεοῦ, ὅταν τὸν Θεὸν ἀγαπῶμεν καὶ τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ ποιῶμεν.
5:2.targetText: In this we know that we love the children of God, when we may love God and may keep His commands;

groups.note: Actual genitive article and first God name jointly supply of God as the children qualifier. The later accusative God object keeps its separate actual occurrence.
The actual ποιῶμεν means do/perform: doing His commands is rendered contextually as keeping them. This is not a claim that the source here contains τηρέω, which is the distinct actual verb in 5:3.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

5:3.sourceText: αὕτη γάρ ἐστιν ἡ ἀγάπη τοῦ Θεοῦ, ἵνα τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ τηρῶμεν· καὶ αἱ ἐντολαὶ αὐτοῦ βαρεῖαι οὐκ εἰσίν,
5:3.targetText: for this is the love of God, that we may keep His commands, and His commands are not burdensome;

groups.note: Actual genitive article and God name jointly supply of God as the love qualifier; the following command and keeping occurrences retain their separate anchors.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

5:4.sourceText: ὅτι πᾶν τὸ γεγεννημένον ἐκ τοῦ Θεοῦ νικᾷ τὸν κόσμον· καὶ αὕτη ἐστὶν ἡ νίκη ἡ νικήσασα τὸν κόσμον, ἡ πίστις ἡμῶν.
5:4.targetText: because everyone who is begotten of God overcomes the world, and this is the victory that overcame the world—our faith.

groups.note: The Greek neuter collective πᾶν, everything that has been begotten, is expressed personally as everyone in this context.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

5:5.sourceText: τίς ἐστιν ὁ νικῶν τὸν κόσμον εἰ μὴ ὁ πιστεύων ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ἐστιν ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ;
5:5.targetText: Who is he who is overcoming the world, if not he who is believing that Jesus is the Son of God?

groups.note: Actual genitive article and God name jointly supply of God as the Son qualifier, without treating of as a standalone lexical translation of the article.

5:6.sourceText: οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ ἐλθὼν δι’ ὕδατος καὶ αἵματος, Ἰησοῦς Χριστός· οὐκ ἐν τῷ ὕδατι μόνον, ἀλλ’ ἐν τῷ ὕδατι καὶ ἐν τῷ αἵματι· καὶ τὸ Πνεῦμά ἐστιν τὸ μαρτυροῦν, ὅτι τὸ Πνεῦμά ἐστιν ἡ ἀλήθεια.
5:6.targetText: This One is He who came through water and blood—Jesus the Christ, not in water only, but in the water and the blood; and the Spirit is the [One] testifying, because the Spirit is the truth,

groups.note: English supplies the definite article with the title; the actual source title Χριστός here is anarthrous.
The Greek repeats ἐν before both coordinated water and blood; English expresses the shared preposition once before the water and the blood.

5:7.targetText: because [there] are three who are testifying [[in Heaven: the Father, the Word, and the Holy Spirit, and these three are one;

groups.note: This is the common causal connector. In N1904 its testimony concerns the Spirit, water, and blood; LSV expands the causal statement with the additional heavenly-witness clause and then coordinates the earthly witnesses in English 5:8.

5:9.sourceText: εἰ τὴν μαρτυρίαν τῶν ἀνθρώπων λαμβάνομεν, ἡ μαρτυρία τοῦ Θεοῦ μείζων ἐστίν, ὅτι αὕτη ἐστὶν ἡ μαρτυρία τοῦ Θεοῦ ὅτι μεμαρτύρηκεν περὶ τοῦ Υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ.
5:9.targetText: If we receive the testimony of men, the testimony of God is greater, because this is the testimony of God that He has testified concerning His Son.

groups.note: Actual genitive article and men noun jointly supply of men as the first testimony qualifier. The two later God qualifiers retain their distinct actual occurrences.

5:10.sourceText: ὁ πιστεύων εἰς τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ ἔχει τὴν μαρτυρίαν ἐν αὑτῷ. ὁ μὴ πιστεύων τῷ Θεῷ ψεύστην πεποίηκεν αὐτόν, ὅτι οὐ πεπίστευκεν εἰς τὴν μαρτυρίαν ἣν μεμαρτύρηκεν ὁ Θεὸς περὶ τοῦ Υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ.
5:10.targetText: He who is believing in the Son of God has the testimony in himself; he who is not believing God has made Him a liar, because he has not believed in the testimony that God has testified concerning His Son;

groups.note: Actual genitive article and first God name jointly supply of God as the Son qualifier. The later dative and nominative God occurrences remain independently anchored.

5:11.sourceText: καὶ αὕτη ἐστὶν ἡ μαρτυρία, ὅτι ζωὴν αἰώνιον ἔδωκεν ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῖν, καὶ αὕτη ἡ ζωὴ ἐν τῷ Υἱῷ αὐτοῦ ἐστιν.
5:11.targetText: and this is the testimony, that God gave continuous life to us, and this life is in His Son;

5:12.sourceText: ὁ ἔχων τὸν Υἱὸν ἔχει τὴν ζωήν· ὁ μὴ ἔχων τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ τὴν ζωὴν οὐκ ἔχει.
5:12.targetText: he who is having the Son has life; he who is not having the Son of God does not have life.

groups.note: Actual genitive article and God name jointly supply of God as the second Son qualifier; the two Son and life occurrences remain separate.

5:13.sourceText: Ταῦτα ἔγραψα ὑμῖν ἵνα εἰδῆτε ὅτι ζωὴν ἔχετε αἰώνιον, τοῖς πιστεύουσιν εἰς τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ Υἱοῦ τοῦ Θεοῦ.
5:13.targetText: I wrote these things to you who are believing in the Name of the Son of God, that you may know that you have continuous life, and that you may believe in the Name of the Son of God.

groups.note: Actual genitive article and God name jointly supply of God in the first Name-of-the-Son construction. The additional final English clause remains a separately explained witness addition and receives no borrowed anchors.

5:15.sourceText: καὶ ἐὰν οἴδαμεν ὅτι ἀκούει ἡμῶν ὃ ἐὰν αἰτώμεθα, οἴδαμεν ὅτι ἔχομεν τὰ αἰτήματα ἃ ᾐτήκαμεν ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ.

5:16.sourceText: Ἐάν τις ἴδῃ τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ ἁμαρτάνοντα ἁμαρτίαν μὴ πρὸς θάνατον, αἰτήσει, καὶ δώσει αὐτῷ ζωήν, τοῖς ἁμαρτάνουσιν μὴ πρὸς θάνατον. ἔστιν ἁμαρτία πρὸς θάνατον· οὐ περὶ ἐκείνης λέγω ἵνα ἐρωτήσῃ.

5:18.sourceText: Οἴδαμεν ὅτι πᾶς ὁ γεγεννημένος ἐκ τοῦ Θεοῦ οὐχ ἁμαρτάνει, ἀλλ’ ὁ γεννηθεὶς ἐκ τοῦ Θεοῦ τηρεῖ αὐτόν, καὶ ὁ πονηρὸς οὐχ ἅπτεται αὐτοῦ.
